spine: Explore vs. exploit, in the RL sense (learner's framing, 2026-10-07). EXPLOIT (3 of 4 weekly blocks): what's known to pay (senior→staff, big-tech-bar interviews, AWS, CUDA/inference, Spark), applied to projects the learner already cares about (3D chess) and, ideally, a side income (shipping the 3D chess game). EXPLORE (1 of 4 blocks): interesting topics that might pay off; one that shows evidence gets promoted into exploit. Every exploit lesson pairs with a 3D chess backlog ticket: the learner does the staff-level part (or the code, when the code is the skill); Claude writes the rest.
rules: Continuous, four lanes, one per eng block: Mon staff, Wed tech, Thu interview, Fri interest (`lanes`). Each lane keeps one active course; when it ends the next in that lane activates at once, so the major never runs empty.

Explore/exploit: 3 exploit lanes (staff, tech, interview) and 1 explore lane (interest), so epsilon = 1/4 of eng blocks. Promotion rule: an explore topic moves into the tech lane when it shows pay or demand evidence in catalog.json, or the learner wants to go deep; a tech-lane topic whose evidence fades drops back to explore. Review this at each catalog refresh and log moves in CHANGES.md.

Every staff/tech/interview lesson ends with a REQUIRED rep (interest-lane reps are optional): one ticket from backlog.json with a definition of done. The next lesson in that lane is not written until the rep is shipped (PR/doc link) or explicitly skipped with a reason. This overrides TEACHING-LOG rule 13 (optional homework) for this major only, at the learner's request (2026-10-07).

Division of labor (learner's rule): Claude writes the code; the learner does the staff-level work (design docs, ADRs, decisions, prioritization, PR review and merge). When the lesson's skill is the code itself (C, C++, CUDA, Spark), the learner writes it and Claude reviews.
Re-check a ticket's GitHub state before assigning it; never file a 'proposed' ticket without asking.
Vim (learner's request, 2026-10-07): every eng lesson opens with a 2-minute Practical Vim drill, and reps are edited in Vim (VI100).
